small_guidance:
- Add larger/wider GEMM autotune configs tuned for M=N=K=8192 + fp32 on Ada (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=4 stages=4, BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=4 stages=5); the current best is likely 128x256 which over-spills registers in fp32. Also try GROUP_M=4 and GROUP_M=16.
- Allow tf32 in the GEMM by passing `allow_tf32=True` to `tl.dot` (and ensure inputs are contiguous fp32) — this typically gives ~2x on Ada for fp32 matmul with negligible accuracy loss for the 5e-2 tolerance.
- For softmax, since N=8192 fits, switch to a single-pass persistent kernel with BLOCK_N=8192 loaded once into registers (num_warps=16 or 8, stages=2) instead of two-pass tile loop; this halves DRAM traffic on the softmax stage.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the row-wise softmax into the matmul epilogue via a split-K / persistent design: have one program own a full row tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N), accumulate the GEMM across K, do GELU on the accumulator, then run online-softmax across N tiles in registers/SMEM and store normalized outputs — eliminating the entire intermediate write/read of the (1024, 8192) post-GELU tensor.
- Alternatively, use a two-stage persistent design: stage 1 streams the GEMM tiles per row group and writes both the GELU output and per-row (max, sum) to small auxiliaries; stage 2 is a lightweight normalize-only kernel doing one read + one write. This avoids needing the whole row resident in one CTA.
- Consider fp16/bf16 compute for the matmul (cast weight once at init, accumulate in fp32) to unlock tensor-core throughput on the 4090 — the dominant cost here is the 8192³ fp32 GEMM, and tf32 or bf16 will move the needle far more than softmax tweaks.
